pipeline.emptyBody: Every ticket travels through these stages, each run by its own AI in its own container. Add your first stage to define what happens first (e.g. Refine or Plan).
pipeline.automationsIntro: Automations react to pipeline events (a ticket created, a stage completed, a cron) and fire an action — a notification, a stage start, an agent. Create your first trigger.
pipeline.systemPromptHint: The base identity + reasoning style for this stage's agent — layered above your instructions.
pipeline.systemPromptPlaceholder: e.g. You are a staff engineer producing a rigorous implementation plan.
pipeline.definitionOfDoneHint: When is this stage complete? Empty = the AI judges completion itself.
pipeline.definitionOfDonePlaceholder: e.g. Every acceptance criterion has a passing test.
pipeline.customInstructionsHint: Loaded into the stage's CLAUDE.md — domain rules + per-stage goals.
pipeline.customInstructionsPlaceholder: e.g. Follow the plan exactly. Keep changes surgical.
pipeline.statusesHint: Base statuses are always present. “Stopped” is set when you stop all AIs or the subscription limit is hit. Add custom chips for this stage.
pipeline.contextDocsHint: Loaded into the container once, read-only.
pipeline.skillsMcpHint: Queried on demand. Frozen-per-commit or live.
pipeline.title: Title
pipeline.descriptionPlaceholder: What this command does + why it's allowed
pipeline.commandPermissionsHint: Pick the commands this stage may run — Allow runs silently, Ask prompts, Deny blocks (deny wins). Hover ? for what each does. Maps to .claude permission rules.
pipeline.integrationsHint: Pick which workspace integration tools this stage may use. Only tools set to write access are mounted at all — a tool left on read-only reaches the AI in no form. Configure tools in Workspace settings → Integrations.
pipeline.noIntegrationTools: No integration tools configured for this workspace yet.
pipeline.visibleToStagesHint: Which stages can read this stage via the cross-ticket skill. The source stage controls its own visibility.
pipeline.containerProcessesHint: What boots in the stage's container — where it runs (working dir), its env vars, and the ordered commands. Stack-agnostic.
pipeline.noProcesses: No processes — nothing starts in the container for this stage.
pipeline.carryFlowInject: the next stage opens with it
pipeline.outgoingEmitHint: This shape is fixed and composed for you - there is nothing to fill in. Every value arrives marked as untrusted text from the previous AI and is cut off at 6,000 characters.
pipeline.automationsMoved: Automations moved to their own page
pipeline.letAgentPickModel: Let the agent pick the model
pipeline.letAgentPickModelDesc: The agent rates the task 1–10 and chooses the highest matching band below — and may escalate itself upward mid-task.
pipeline.escalationBandsHint: if task score ≥ N → use this model / effort / turns. Highest match wins; the bottom band is the default that catches everything else.
pipeline.contextBudgetHint: When a session's estimated tokens cross this, the AI writes a handoff and resets — blank uses the default.
pipeline.networkEgressDesc: Off = the container has no internet at all.
pipeline.whitelistDesc: Everything is blocked except the categories + hosts below (locked-down).
pipeline.blacklistDesc: Everything is allowed except the categories + hosts below (open).
pipeline.hostsPrefixesHint: Exact hosts or wildcard prefixes, e.g. registry.npmjs.org or *.github.com.
pipeline.lifecycleHooksHint: Hooks POST to the orchestrator — they power the event-log, status tracking and needs-input escalation. Disabling them blinds those features.

pipeline.warnWriteAccess: {{name}} has write access to a service — usually only Implementatie needs that.

pipeline.warnRagMismatch: Refined loads RAG but Plan does not — the decision stage usually needs more context, not less.

pipeline.presetSwitchMoves: {{count}} ticket(s) move back to the nearest earlier stage that still exists.
pipeline.presetSwitchKeepsCustom: Stages you added yourself are kept.
pipeline.aiSkillsHint: The instruction blocks this stage's agent runs with. Off means this stage skips it; other stages keep theirs.
pipeline.aiSkillsTipBody: A skill is written once under AI > Skills and switched on here, so a plan stage and a review stage can run with different instructions.

pipeline.remoteUpdated: This stage was changed elsewhere while you were editing.
pipeline.discardEdits: Discard my edits and load it

automations.approvalBody: With this on, the rule stops running by itself: it puts a request in the Suggestions tab of the AI panel and only does the work once someone accepts it. Leaving it off is no guarantee of a direct run — shell commands, and agent roles that change things, are always held for approval anyway.
automations.chatBody: Answers are built from the live workspace: the selected project's own details, its tickets, stages and members, plus whatever has been indexed of its code, knowledge about this platform and lessons saved earlier in this workspace. Without a code index only the code excerpts are left out — the rest of the answer still applies. A project must be selected: without one, the chat cannot answer at all.
automations.chatIndexPoint: Index this project's code on the Sources page
automations.cronBody: The schedule is checked once a minute in the workspace's own time zone, Amsterdam time — not your device's time and not UTC. There is no screen anywhere to change that. A rule is only checked while its switch is on.
automations.debounceBody: Events that arrive during the waiting time are thrown away, not queued — they never run later. The clock also restarts on a run that only asked for approval, so a request nobody accepts still blocks all of those seconds. Schedules are never affected.
automations.findingsSeverityDesc: It is not a judgement about impact: every security or reliability idea is marked high, and no other kind ever is.
automations.findingsSourceDesc: Nothing you ask in the chat is ever saved here, however useful the answer is. A scheduled rule can produce findings too, which is why some appear that nobody asked for. The list belongs to the whole workspace, so it also holds findings made while another project was selected.
automations.findingsTicketDesc: There is no confirmation step: a ticket appears on the board of the selected project, at the first stage, with high priority when the finding is high. With no project selected the button quietly does nothing.
automations.ideasBody: This starts a review of the selected project in the background. There is no progress bar on purpose — the ideas simply appear in the findings list a while later. Everyone in the workspace gets a notification when it finishes, so this is not a private action.
automations.matchStageBody: This is checked against the stage the event itself reports, never the stage the ticket sits in right now. A newly created ticket always reports one fixed stage, whatever your pipeline looks like, so at most one choice here ever matches it. An accepted suggestion or a signal reports no stage at all, so any stage filter stops those rules from ever firing.
automations.matchStageHelp: Filters on the stage the event itself reports, not the stage the ticket is in right now.
automations.noRoles: No agent roles are available. Roles come from the server this app runs on, not from this workspace — ask whoever runs the server to enable one.
automations.noStages: This project has no pipeline stages yet, so there is nothing to move a ticket into.
automations.runNowBody: Running a rule by hand starts it without a ticket, so anything that needs one — moving a ticket to a stage, running a command — does nothing at all. And when the rule needs approval, this button only puts an approval request in the AI panel instead of running it.

backlog.approvalBody: Because this role changes things, the timer never does the work itself. Every run files an approval request under Suggestions in the AI panel, and the work only happens once someone accepts it there. "Run now" does exactly the same.
backlog.approvalTitle: This role waits for a person
backlog.channelsPointDesc: Only the idea generator really runs once per channel. Every other role receives your selection and ignores it.
backlog.clockBody: Times are read in the workspace's own time zone, not the one on your phone or laptop. That zone is fixed when the workspace is created and cannot be changed anywhere in the app, so 09:00 here may be a different hour where you are.
backlog.countBody: The first number counts the tickets shown here, which never include archived ones. The second counts every ticket in the workspace, archived ones included. So once you archive something, the first number stays lower even after you clear every filter.
backlog.focusPointDesc: Only the interviewer role reads this text; for the other roles it changes nothing.
backlog.lastRunBody: It is the last time the task actually did something (or filed a request for approval) — not the last time the timer went off. A run that fails, or that has nothing to do, leaves this time untouched, so it can stay hours old while the task keeps firing.
backlog.newTicketBody: Whatever you fill in, a ticket created here starts in the first stage, Unrefined, with no AI on it — it waits there until someone moves it on. From the board a ticket can be started with AI right away; here every ticket also always gets normal priority.
backlog.noChannelsLabel: No content channels yet, so there is nothing to spread this task over.
backlog.noRolesLabel: No AI roles are available in this installation, so this task can only send a notification.
backlog.noStagesLabel: This project has no pipeline stages, so tickets cannot be moved anywhere.
backlog.personBody: A ticket is kept when the chosen person created it or is assigned to it. You therefore see their own work mixed with everything they merely filed — and picking yourself in a workspace where you created everything filters nothing out.
backlog.unrefinedBody: It does not look at a ticket's status: it shows the tickets sitting in the pipeline stage "unrefined". Renaming that stage does not rename this chip, and even deleting the stage does not change what the chip finds — those tickets stay where they are and new tickets usually still start there, they simply no longer belong to any column on the board.
backlog.unrefinedStagePoint: The stage this chip reads from

board.approveNoteBody: Approve and Reject are not a separate verdict the system understands: they send the word “Approved” or “Rejected” as your written answer, with your note added after a colon. Nothing reacts to the word itself — your answer is usually passed on to the AI as it carries on. So write the note as something you want it to do.
board.approveNoteTitle: Your note goes straight to the AI
board.artifactsEmpty: No designs or Studio artifacts yet
board.artifactsModulesOff: Designer and Studio are switched off in this workspace, so there is nothing to attach
board.capacitySourceBody: The maximum is set on the server (the WS_MAX_CONCURRENT_TURNS setting, 4 by default) and cannot be changed inside the app. It is also shared by every workspace on this server, so work someone starts elsewhere takes up the same slots and can push your tickets into the queue.
board.moreOpenGateBody: Answering this one does not restart the ticket. It stays parked and waiting, and the next open question simply takes this one's place. Only once every question has an answer does the ticket start moving again, with all your answers passed on together.
board.moreOpenGateTitle: The AI resumes only after the last answer
board.newTicketStartBody: Every new ticket lands in Unrefined, where the AI is switched off — it will simply wait there. It only starts when you open Options below and tick “Start with AI right away”, or when you later move the card to another stage from the card's ⋯ menu.
board.quickAddParkedBody: This quick-add field has no options, so the ticket stays in Unrefined and no agent will ever pick it up — this column is meant for your own triage. To have the AI start on it, use “+ Ticket” at the top and tick “Start with AI right away”, or move the card to another stage when you are ready.
board.quickAddParkedTitle: This ticket will just sit here

code.emptyTree: This repository is linked, but no files came back — it most likely has no commits yet.
code.mirrorCopy: The server keeps its own copy of the repository
code.mirrorCopyDesc: The branch name and the files below it are read from that copy, not from your Git host right now. It is also the copy Workspaces itself works in, so a merge or a rollback it carries out on this branch lands there too.
code.mirrorRefresh: Commits pushed from outside stay invisible
code.mirrorRefreshDesc: Work that reaches your Git host another way — a colleague, a build server, a push from your own machine — is never picked up here on its own.
code.mirrorRelink: Linking the repository again starts the copy over
code.mirrorRelinkDesc: It is the only way to bring outside work in, but it fetches the repository from scratch: anything that lived only in the copy here is lost.
code.scopeBody: Two things you cannot see on this screen determine the contents of the file tree.
code.scopeCapDesc: A very large repository is cut off at 5,000 files without any warning on screen, so a missing file may simply fall past that limit.
code.scopeProject: The project selected in the top bar
code.scopeProjectDesc: Every project has its own repository, so switching project swaps the entire codebase shown here.
code.scopeTitle: What decides which files you see
code.termShellAgent: The AI is working in here too
code.termShellAgentDesc: Whatever you change, install or delete is immediately what the AI sees while it works on this ticket.
code.termShellBody: This is not a safe scratch shell: it opens inside the very container the AI works in, in the same folder.
code.termShellPush: Only committed work reaches your Git host
code.termShellPushDesc: Changes you leave here without committing them go nowhere. A commit on the ticket's branch only leaves this container when the AI finishes a stage — and not every workspace pushes to a Git host at all.
code.termShellTitle: You are typing in the ticket's real container
code.termTabsBody: Each tab is a container running right now for a ticket in this workspace — it is not a list of your tickets.
code.termTabsPollDesc: Tabs can appear or vanish on their own, and if the container service is unreachable they all disappear at once.
code.termTabsRunning: Containers started for a ticket get a tab
code.termTabsRunningDesc: Not only a pipeline step: the code editor, a preview, a checks run or a deployment each start one too, so a tab can carry a name that is not one of your tickets. A tab disappears once its container stops.

content.autopilotApprovalDesc: Anyone publishing a piece on this channel skips the approval step, instead of waiting for someone to accept it first.
content.autopilotBody: Turning it on approves publishing on this channel in advance.
content.autopilotChainDesc: If an idea task names this channel, idea, script, media and publishing all run without asking you per step.
content.autopilotOwner: It runs as the workspace owner
content.autopilotOwnerDesc: However that chain is started, it acts with the workspace owner's identity.
content.budgetLimitsBlockedDesc: A refused generation creates no file, costs nothing and is not retried. Start it again yourself once there is room.
content.budgetLimitsBody: Your own cap is not always the only limit.
content.budgetLimitsHost: A server-wide ceiling, if there is one
content.budgetLimitsHostDesc: Whoever runs this server can cap all workspaces together. Usually there is none, but when one is set, a new generation may be refused once that total is reached — even without a cap of your own.
content.budgetLimitsTitle: What else can stop a generation
content.budgetSourceBody: Counting starts once a media budget has been set up.
content.budgetSourceLifetimeDesc: From then on it simply keeps running: this is not this month's spend, and changing the cap leaves the number untouched.
content.budgetSourceNoBudget: Without a budget it stays at €0.00
content.budgetSourceNoBudgetDesc: As long as no media budget has been set up, nothing is counted here, however much you generate. What everything has cost in total is on Insights.
content.budgetSourceStubDesc: Without a provider key nothing is really generated, but the placeholder that comes back is still booked at the normal estimate.
content.disclosureAutoDesc: Nobody ticks anything, so exactly this setting is what the platform is told about AI-generated media.
content.disclosureBody: The same setting, two very different roles.
content.disclosureManualDesc: It only pre-ticks the box in the publish form; whatever you leave there is what gets sent.
content.noAccounts: No account connected for this platform yet — connect one under "Publishing connections" below.
content.noLivePieces: No active pieces — everything is archived, so there is nothing to add this to.
content.noStyles: No house styles yet — a style is the look the AI reuses for this channel.

designer.actionsBody: 'Use in project' saves the previewed theme or style and makes it the workspace's active design system: from the next run on, the coding agent is told to build with it. It does not change a single file in your repository.
designer.activeNameBody: This is the look that is saved as the workspace's design system, not the one in the preview picker above. They can differ: your preview stays on your own screen until you press 'Use in project'.
designer.applyTokensDesc: The only action that writes code: it rewrites the managed colour block in the project's src/index.css and commits that file to your target branch. It uses the saved active theme, not the preview, and stops with an error instead of overwriting anything unexpected.
designer.compareNeedsProject: No project selected yet — a comparison is filed against a project, so Compare stays unavailable until there is one.
designer.feedbackNeedsProject: No project selected yet — a UI review belongs to a project. You cannot send a new request, and an older request without a project cannot become a ticket.
designer.generateBody: The result is added to the list on this screen only. Refresh the page or switch workspace and it is gone. Keep it with 'Use in project' or 'Save to library' — for an animation, use the Save button in the Animations section.
designer.noLiveEnv: Nothing is deployed yet — once this project has a live environment, you can fill 'our page' with its address in one tap.
designer.previewThemeBody: Picking a theme here changes nothing on its own — it only restyles what you see, and not everywhere: the Themes, Styles and Typography tabs follow it, the Gallery shows each look in its own colours (only the light/dark switch changes those), and Animations follows neither control. On the Themes tab this is also the theme that 'Use in project' and 'Save to library' store, so choose it here before you press either.
designer.saveToLibraryDesc: Keeps the look so you can come back to it later, without making it the active one.

documents.aiSourcesBody: Your instruction is only part of it. Every mode runs on the last saved version, so anything you typed but have not saved — a new title too — is left out. Save first. 'Generate' writes fresh text instead of reworking what is already there.
documents.aiSourcesDocsDesc: Up to six matching excerpts from the other documents in this workspace, plus a little product knowledge.
documents.aiSourcesFilesDesc: The text of every attached pdf, Word or text file read successfully — used only up to a point, and less of it the more you attach.
documents.aiSourcesTemplateDesc: If this document was made from a template, the AI is told to follow that section list exactly — what comes back is still a draft you check.
documents.aiSourcesTitle: What the AI draft is built from
documents.aiSourcesWorkspaceDesc: The workspace instruction, the output language and every switched-on skill apply to every draft.
documents.archiveBody: Archived documents only disappear from this list. Their history stays, and their content can still be used when the AI drafts your other documents. They do drop out of the assistant's chat right away. Only Delete really removes a document, its history and everything the AI could still quote from it.
documents.exportBody: The file is made from the version stored on the server, so anything you have not saved yet is missing from it — press Save first. Word and PDF are rendered by Docker on the server and fail without it. Your workspace logo appears in HTML and PDF only. Excel gets one sheet per table in the document; without tables you get a single column of lines.
documents.restoreBody: The version you have now is saved into the history first, so a restore can itself be undone. But an AI draft you have not applied yet is thrown away at the same moment — apply or copy it before you restore.
documents.reuseEmptyLabel: No images to reuse yet — images you create under Content show up here, free to attach.
documents.templateBody: A template does more than fill in headings. The document keeps that choice for life — nothing in the app clears it — and later AI drafts are asked to follow those sections, though what comes back is still a draft you check and apply; your own text is never rearranged on its own. Editing or deleting one of your own templates changes what its documents' next drafts are asked for — the documents themselves stay as they are.
documents.uploadBody: Pdf, Word, txt and markdown files are first read out into text: a clock means still busy, a warning triangle means reading failed (pdf and Word need Docker on the server). A file that turns out to hold no readable text — a scanned pdf, say — keeps the plain file icon but still gives the AI nothing. Only files that were read successfully feed this document's AI drafts, and they stay with this document: your other documents never see them. An uploaded image is attached for display only — the document AI never looks at it.

insights.activityWindowBody: This feed holds only the 50 most recent events in the workspace. These buttons narrow that list — they never search further back, so People or Merges can look empty while older events of that kind still exist.
insights.activityWindowTitle: The filter works on the last 50 events
insights.contentCostBody: This adds up what generating images, video, audio and voice cost in this workspace. What the writing AI costs is not included. It also still counts spend on pieces you archived, while the counts beside it leave archived pieces out.
insights.contentCostLlmDesc: Sits on the Usage page, with its own caps.
insights.cycleTimeBody: A ticket records no completion moment, so this is the time between when it was created and when it was last changed — over this project's non-archived tickets that are marked Done. Any later change to a Done ticket stretches its number afterwards (a comment does not), and archiving it removes it from the average.
insights.cycleTimeTitle: Measured from creation to last change
insights.enforcementAria: What the two pause options do
insights.enforcementBody: As soon as a switched-on cap reaches its amount, new AI runs on tickets stop starting — by the pipeline or by hand — while runs already going are left to finish. Other AI features and media generation keep going and keep spending; media has its own separate budget. Choosing between the two options changes nothing; runs only start again once every switched-on cap is back under its amount.
insights.enforcementTitle: Both options do the same thing today
insights.graphEdgesBody: Lines are not connections anyone drew. Items are compared on their text, and a line appears once they resemble each other enough. Each item offers at most four matches of its own, so some items get fewer lines and one that many others resemble can get more. The stronger the resemblance, the more solid the line.
insights.graphNodesBody: Only context sources that are switched on, tickets that are not archived, and content pieces. Sources often start out off, so they are missing here until someone turns them on; archiving a ticket drops it at the next refresh. Archiving does not remove a content piece, nor a source that is still switched on. Very large workspaces are cut off at 100 sources, the 200 most recently active tickets and 100 pieces.
insights.graphNodesSourcesDesc: The switch sits in a source's details, labelled AI-editable.
insights.graphNodesTitle: Not everything in the workspace is here
insights.graphRefreshBody: It reads every item again and compares them all from scratch. With a Gemini key set that is a paid call: it appears in the AI activity log and counts towards the euro caps. Without a key it uses a free local comparison, which matches on shared words instead of on meaning.
insights.graphRefreshCapsDesc: In the workspace's spend caps on the Usage page.
insights.noChannelsLabel: No channels yet, so there is no brand voice to show.
insights.noPiecesLabel: No content pieces yet — links made here stand on their own, they are not tied to a piece.
insights.noStylesLabel: No styles yet — this list stays empty until someone adds one.
insights.publishedBody: One piece sent to three channels counts three times, and publishing the same piece again adds another. That is why this number can be higher than Done or than the total number of pieces.
insights.resumeSpendBody: Not only the budget beside it: every cap on this page drops back to zero and starts a new period from now, so ticket work these caps were blocking can start again — unless a server-wide limit set by whoever hosts this is reached as well.
insights.resumeSpendMediaDesc: Generating images, video, audio and voice has its own cap in the content settings. If that one is full, this button does not free it.
insights.resumeSpendMediaLabel: The media budget stays as it is
insights.resumeSpendTitle: This resets every cap on this page
insights.spendWindowBody: Each cap adds up everything spent since its own period opened. A period opens when the cap is created and when someone presses Resume spend — nothing else resets it, so a period can run for months.
insights.spendWindowSharedDesc: All caps are scored against the whole workspace's paid spend. A cap's name describes it; it does not limit what it counts.
insights.spendWindowSharedLabel: Every cap measures the same spend
insights.tokenEstimateAria: Where these token numbers come from
insights.tokenEstimateBody: The coding assistant reports no usage of its own, so tokens are estimated from how much text went in and out (roughly four characters per token). That work runs on the subscription and costs nothing extra here. Only providers that charge per token deliver real numbers.
insights.tokenEstimateTitle: These are estimates, not a bill
insights.winnerBody: It is not the winner of one test: every link in the workspace competes in the same ranking, whatever campaign it belongs to. A click is one visit to the link, counted without any filtering, so bots and link previews count too.

piece.costBody: The amount on the button is what one generated video clip costs. A full video is made of one clip per scene, so the real total is this amount multiplied by the number of scenes.
piece.costExtras: Script and voice-over come on top
piece.costExtrasDesc: The spoken track adds a couple of cents; writing the script is not part of this media price.
piece.costScenes: The length decides the number of scenes
piece.costScenesDesc: Roughly one scene per 5 seconds — about 4 scenes for short, 9 for normal and 18 for long. You set the length under Output settings.
piece.costTitle: This is the price of one clip
piece.directionBody: The script is not written from this box alone. The workspace first hands the AI everything it already knows about your product and your channel, and your text is appended at the end — so it fine-tunes instead of replacing.
piece.directionBrandDesc: What you make and for whom, stored once per workspace.
piece.directionDocsDesc: Only documents that are switched on and not archived are used.
piece.directionVoiceDesc: The tone of the channel this piece belongs to.
piece.failedAttempts: Three attempts, further apart each time
piece.failedAttemptsDesc: About five minutes after the first failure and about ten after the second — longer when the error mentions a rate limit.
piece.failedBody: A post only gets this badge after the third failed attempt. The first two failures are invisible here: the post looks like a normal upcoming post, gets a later time and is tried again.
piece.failedNotifyDesc: A notification appeared in the app when the post finally failed, plus a push message on devices where push is set up and switched on.
piece.styleBody: Every style was made for one step of the production: the script, the voice-over, the images or the video scenes. Only that step uses your pick — the other steps carry on without it, and this list does not show which step a style belongs to.
piece.styleEmpty: No styles yet — a style stores a look or tone you reuse on every generation.
piece.styleStep: Picking the wrong one does nothing
piece.styleStepDesc: A style written for the script changes the wording, not the look of the video.
piece.styleTitle: A style belongs to one step
piece.styleWhere: See which step each style is for
piece.styleWhereDesc: Brand & styles shows the step next to every style.
piece.templateAspectDesc: The template's own format (16:9, 9:16 or 1:1) wins, and its watermark position is applied as well.
piece.templateBody: The big "Generate full video" button ignores this choice. A template is only applied when you run Assemble under "More generations" — and it then replaces the aspect ratio you picked here with its own.
piece.templateEmpty: No output templates yet — a template fixes the aspect ratio and watermark of a render.
piece.templateTitle: A template only works via Assemble
piece.timeBody: The app checks about once a minute which posts are due. The time you see can move on its own, so a post rarely goes out at exactly the minute shown.
piece.timeRetry: A failed upload is tried again twice
piece.timeRetryDesc: It goes back in the queue with a later time. If the third attempt fails too, the time stops moving and the post is marked failed.
piece.timeStagger: A burst to the same account is spread out
piece.timeStaggerDesc: When several posts to the same account come due at once, one goes out and the rest are pushed back roughly five minutes apart.
piece.timeTitle: This time is the earliest moment
piece.timelineAssetsEmpty: No finished video or image in this piece yet — generate or import one and you can add it here as a scene.

pipeline.commandsBaselineBody: These rows shape what the AI does; they are not a lock. Inside its own container the stage works without permission prompts, so it can also run commands you left on Off, and Ask never actually stops to ask — nobody is sitting at that terminal. What really contains a stage is that container: isolated, without access to your own computer, and thrown away when the work is done.
pipeline.contextDocsBody: Ticking documents here adds to what this stage receives; it does not limit it. Starter documents and the workspace-wide design-system document usually travel along too. Archived documents are never sent. This list carries at most 12 documents, each shortened to its first 4,000 characters, and when more qualify the order is not fixed — so keep the selection small. On top of this list the stage still receives other material, such as the output of earlier stages and documents linked to the ticket.
pipeline.escalationScoreBody: The score is not calculated by Workspaces, and this stage does not grade itself. The AI of the previous stage estimates on a scale of 1 to 10 how complex the remaining work is and passes that number on. This stage then picks, once at its start, the band with the highest threshold that number reaches. Without a number — the first stage, or the previous AI left it out — the bands are skipped and the fallback is used.
pipeline.noDocs: No context documents in this project yet.
pipeline.noSkills: Skills and MCP tools are capabilities the AI calls on demand. Nothing in the app creates one yet, and indexing the repository will not fill this list either.
pipeline.toolTierBody: Read does not give the stage limited access — it gives none at all. Only Write actually hands the tool to the stage; with Read the tool is not installed in the container, because an outside tool cannot be forced to stay read-only. Switching a tool on selects Read by default, so choose Write if the stage really needs it.
pipeline.toolTierTitle: Read means the tool is left out entirely
pipeline.validateLocalBody: Despite the name, no AI is involved and nothing leaves your browser. Workspaces checks the stages on screen against five fixed rules and lists what it finds. It judges what is on screen right now, including changes you have not saved yet.
pipeline.validateLocalTitle: This check runs in your browser
pipeline.noSkillsAlt: Written instructions the AI should follow are a different thing, confusingly also called Skills — and those you can create:
pipeline.handoverTitle: Written at the end, not the start
pipeline.handoverBody: This is the one editable half of the carry-over. It runs when this stage finishes and tells it what to put in the summary the next stage opens with. There is nothing to configure on the receiving end: the previous stage's summary, changed files, open questions and pinned commit are composed for you, each marked as untrusted text from another AI. Leave this empty and the AI judges for itself what matters - which is usually fine, and worth overriding when a specific stage needs a specific thing.

settings.dbEnvBody: This single choice steers two things: the connection you save here, and the environment a new migration is written for.
settings.dbEnvProdDesc: A migration written for production only runs after you confirm it and after a rollback script has been stored with it. This form cannot store one yet, so a production migration created here stays pending.
settings.dbEnvReplaceDesc: Connecting while this environment already has a database replaces those saved details instead of adding a second one — without a warning and without an undo.
settings.demoBody: Leave the commit field empty and the demo follows your main branch: about once a minute the app checks whether the branch moved and re-deploys the demo if it did. Fill it in and the demo freezes on that commit and stops following. Only the demo does this.
settings.demoDnsDesc: The subdomain and the custom domain are checked against every environment on this server. If one is already taken, what you typed is thrown away without any warning and the demo keeps its own generated address.
settings.demoDnsLabel: An address already in use is dropped silently
settings.envBody: Every button in this card acts on the project selected in the top bar, and does nothing when no project is selected.
settings.envChecksDesc: If this project runs automatic builds, a promotion to production is refused when the checks for that exact version failed, are still running, or belong to a different version, or when a serious security issue was found for it. Without such builds, no check here can refuse it.
settings.envChecksLabel: Automatic checks only guard you once you use them
settings.envProdDesc: The only route into production is a promotion from staging, and it always asks you to confirm first. A deploy aimed straight at production is refused.
settings.envPromoteDesc: Promote moves one step up a fixed ladder — dev to staging, staging to production — and re-deploys the exact version that is live in the environment you promote from, not the newest code on your branch.
settings.envPromoteLabel: Promote ships what is already running
settings.forgeConnectedBody: Green only means your details were saved — they are never tested. A wrong token, address or repository path shows exactly the same badge, and you find out when a job that needs the repository fails. The token is stored encrypted, per project.
settings.noMigrations: No migrations yet. One you write in the form above appears here, waiting to be applied.
settings.noProjectDb: Connecting a database needs a project. Without one the Connect button looks active but does nothing at all — create a project from the menu in the top bar first.
settings.noProjectEnvs: Deploying needs a project. These buttons act on the project chosen in the top bar — create one there first.
settings.noProjectForge: There is no project yet, so there is nothing to link a repository to. Create one from the project menu in the top bar first.
settings.noServices: This project has no separate services. A project made of several parts — an app and an API, say — can deploy each part on its own once you add them under “Add service” in the project menu at the top.
settings.servicesBody: Besides starting the containers, a successful start can save the connection details in this workspace's environment variables — encrypted, and labelled with this stack's name.
settings.servicesClashDesc: The details are stored under ordinary names such as the database or mail address, so an entry you already had under that name is replaced without a warning. Removing the stack then deletes those entries, including the one it replaced — your old value does not come back.
settings.servicesClashLabel: It can overwrite what you already had
settings.servicesCustomDesc: Whether a Compose file you paste in yourself saves any connection details depends on how the stack is run, so check your environment variables afterwards instead of assuming either way.
settings.servicesCustomLabel: Your own Compose file may save nothing

sources.aiEditableBody: It decides whether this document's text is given to the AI. It is not permission to edit the file — nothing in the app treats it that way.
sources.aiEditableDefaultDesc: A document you upload or scan from the repository is switched off, so the AI does not use it until you turn it on here.
sources.aiEditableNotALockDesc: A pipeline stage that names this document under Context & Skills loads it anyway, switched off or not.
sources.codeIndexAfterReloadDesc: When you open this page there are no numbers yet, so it reads as not indexed even when the index is complete. Start a reindex from the maintenance menu to see the real figures.
sources.codeIndexAfterSwitch: It does not follow a switch
sources.codeIndexAfterSwitchDesc: The numbers stay on screen when you switch project or workspace, so they can still describe the one you just left.
sources.codeIndexAria: Where the code index status comes from
sources.codeIndexBody: These numbers arrive as a live update when a reindex is run from the app — by you, a teammate, or the assistant. Nothing looks them up on its own.
sources.scopeAria: Why a document or skill may be missing from these lists
sources.scopeBody: Both lists are filtered the same way: you see what belongs to the whole workspace, plus what belongs to the project you have open. In practice mainly a project's starter documents are tied to it. A switch only filters the list; nothing is deleted.
sources.scopeTitle: Why something may be missing here
sources.skillsNone: No skills or MCP tools. Nothing in the app can create one yet, so reindexing the code will not fill this list.
sources.stagesAria: Why this stage list can be empty
sources.stagesBody: These labels are recorded once, when the document is created, and nothing updates them afterwards. So an empty list does not mean no stage reads this document: what actually decides is each stage's own Context & Skills selection in the pipeline.
sources.stagesTitle: What this list is, and is not

studio.actionsBody: Each one hands the result to another part of the app, and the labels do not say where it ends up.
studio.actionsBrandDesc: Overwrites the workspace brand library with this card's colours, fonts, voice and taglines — you confirm on a before-and-after list first.
studio.actionsContentDesc: Creates a new content piece with this card attached, in your content project — and creates a project called Content if you do not have one yet.
studio.actionsPublishDesc: Puts this page on a public web address. Publishing the same card again updates that same page, but the app does not show you the address anywhere yet.
studio.actionsTitle: These buttons change things outside this card
studio.brandGateBody: As soon as the brand library holds one colour or a voice, it is pasted into the prompt of every asset you generate, for every brief. Remove all the colours and empty the voice and it stops being used.
studio.brandGateLabel: How the brand library affects generating
studio.brandGateSentDesc: The colours with their hex codes, the heading and body font, the voice and any taglines you saved.
studio.brandGateTitle: This is a switch, not a shelf
studio.brandGateVoice: If you leave the voice empty
studio.brandGateVoiceDesc: The tone from the brief is used as the voice instead.
studio.promptExtrasBody: This preview shows only what you set on this page. Three more things are attached automatically, which is usually why a result comes back in an unexpected language or tone.
studio.promptExtrasKnowledgeDesc: Two short snippets about what this platform can do are looked up and attached, so the result can point you at a sensible next step.
studio.promptExtrasLabel: What else is added to this prompt
studio.promptExtrasLanguageDesc: The output language and the standing AI instruction of this workspace are placed in front of every generation.
studio.promptExtrasSkillsDesc: Every enabled skill that applies to Studio adds its own instructions, so switching one on changes the register of everything generated here.
studio.promptExtrasTitle: More is added before the AI reads this
studio.regenerateBody: It never replaces the card you started from. You get a second card next to it, and the first one stays here until you delete it yourself.
studio.regenerateLabel: What regenerating does to this list
studio.regeneratePublishedDesc: The live page is not updated by regenerating. The new card is a separate page with its own web address, so publish that card too and share the new link.
studio.regenerateRefineClearedDesc: After every run the refine box on this page is cleared, so pressing the same button again runs without it unless you type it in once more.

ticket.artifactsBody: Links are read each time the AI starts working, so they never change work that is already running. Only the eight oldest links are read; anything above that is skipped, and long designs and specifications are shortened.
ticket.artifactsEmpty: There is no design or specification yet to link. Create one first, then the AI builds to it.
ticket.artifactsTitle: Read at the start of a turn
ticket.previewBody: It starts this ticket's own version of the app in its own container, not a shared test site. Two things decide whether that works.
ticket.previewBranchDesc: Until the AI has picked the ticket up and made its own working copy, there is nothing to show and the preview stops right away.
ticket.previewCmdDesc: You do not have to set a start command yourself: without one, a standard command for the project's technology is used, which usually works. If the preview does not come up, set your own command.
ticket.previewTitle: A preview of this ticket only
ticket.priorityBlockedDesc: The AI starts work even when tickets that block this one are still open. Merging still needs your approval.
ticket.priorityBody: Urgent has two effects; the note next to it names only the first.
ticket.priorityQueueDesc: It starts even when the maximum number of tickets is already being worked on at the same time.
ticket.serviceBody: The chosen part decides which folder of the repository a preview starts in; whole project starts at the top. The container and the start command always come from the project itself, also for a part. A preview that is already running keeps its current folder — the change only takes effect once this ticket's container has stopped.
ticket.serviceEmpty: This project has no separate parts yet, so a preview always starts the whole project from the top of the repository. You add parts from the project menu at the top of the screen.
ticket.serviceTitle: It changes more than a label
ticket.stageAiDesc: With No AI the ticket simply stays here: no agent will ever start working on it, whatever else is set.
ticket.stageBody: This shows the settings of the step this ticket is in. You change them on the Pipeline page, not here.
ticket.stageSkillsDesc: The skills listed here do not reach the AI yet: switching one on changes nothing about how it works today. Workspace-level skills are the ones that can reach it.
ticket.stageSourcesDesc: Documents from this project that the AI gets as background. The number counts what is picked for this step, and a step can carry a placeholder pick that is counted but never handed over. Switched-on starter documents and the workspace design guide are usually added too.

workspace.autonomyBody: This setting decides whether a finished stage hands over on its own.
workspace.autonomyEveryDesc: Every stage waits for you, including the ones that are not marked.
workspace.autonomyFullDesc: A finished stage hands over on its own, though not always instantly. A stage marked 'ask for approval' usually still waits for you to start it.
workspace.autonomyKeyDesc: Only the stages you marked in the pipeline editor wait for you.
workspace.autonomyTitle: What this does to stage approvals
workspace.envSecretBody: A secret value never leaves the server, so this box never holds it. What the row can tell you is whether one is stored, and it does — that is the label beside the box.
workspace.envSecretKeepDesc: Saving a secret with an empty box keeps the value that is already stored.
workspace.envSecretReplaceDesc: Whatever you type becomes the new value and is stored encrypted.
workspace.envSecretRevealDesc: An empty secret says "not set" and is directly editable; there is nothing to hide yet.
workspace.mcpAria: What is needed before the AI can use this tool
workspace.mcpBody: Turning it on does not yet give the AI access. Two more things have to be true.
workspace.mcpCommandDesc: Kafka, RabbitMQ, S3, Elasticsearch and HTTP API come without one, and an empty command starts nothing.
workspace.mcpCommandLabel: There has to be a command
workspace.mcpStageDesc: Pick this tool in a pipeline stage and set it to read and write; at read-only it is quietly left out.
workspace.mcpStageLabel: A stage has to allow reading and writing
workspace.mcpTitle: This switch alone is not enough
workspace.noEnvVarsLabel: No environment variables yet, so there is nothing to link these fields to.
workspace.noTransferTargetLabel: There is nobody to hand it over to yet — you are the only member of this workspace.
workspace.permsBody: A tick decides what everyone with that role may do across this workspace, not only on this page. Another workspace has its own ticks.
workspace.permsBuiltinDesc: Owner's cells cannot be clicked, and clicking Admin or Member simply changes nothing: built-in roles are fixed. Add your own role to give people a different set of rights.
workspace.permsBuiltinLabel: Owner, Admin and Member are fixed
workspace.permsInstantDesc: Everyone with that role notices it on their very next action. Nobody has to sign in again.
workspace.permsWidestDesc: It covers around a hundred actions, from ticket work to merging, publishing and spending the AI budget. 'Workspace settings / GitLab token' comes next with about fifty.
workspace.permsWidestLabel: 'Use terminals + work on tickets' is the broadest row

workspaceSettings.customTaskTemplatePlaceholder: Prompt template, e.g. Summarize {{topic}} in 5 bullets

workspaceSettings.starterDescription: Toggle curated conventions the AI follows in every stage. Write your own on the Sources page.

workspaceSettings.name: Name

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: Plain-language definitions of the terms used across the app.
glossary.workspaceDef: Your project's home — holds its tickets, content, settings and team. You can have several.
glossary.moduleDef: A feature lane you enable per workspace: Development (code), Content & Marketing (media), or Design.
glossary.ticketDef: A unit of work (a task, bug or feature). An AI agent picks it up and moves it through the pipeline.
glossary.pipelineDef: The ordered stages a ticket flows through — e.g. refine, plan, implement, test, review.
glossary.stageDef: One column of the pipeline. Each stage has its own AI prompt, tools and definition-of-done.
glossary.mrDef: A proposed code change awaiting review and approval before it merges into your main branch.
glossary.environmentDef: A running deployment of your app at a stable URL (dev, staging, prod or demo).
glossary.pieceDef: One media project — a script, voiceover, images and the rendered video, in the Content module.
glossary.shortlinkDef: A /l/slug link that counts clicks — the conversion signal for an ad or campaign.
